clauses.notes: A policy can name the category. Whether collected data meets the definition is product-level.
clauses.summary: Neural data is information generated by measuring activity of an individual's central or peripheral nervous system, and is included in biological data.

clauses.notes: Observable if the policy lists neural data as sensitive personal information.
clauses.summary: Neural data is classified as sensitive data under the Colorado Privacy Act.

clauses.notes: Policy may claim consent. Actual consent UX is network_or_product.
clauses.summary: A controller shall not process sensitive data without consent.
A consumer may request deletion of personal data.

clauses.notes: Phase 0 schema does not encode an access-right field. Unmeasured as a field.
clauses.summary: A consumer may confirm processing of personal data and access it.

clauses.notes: Phase 0 schema does not encode a correction-right field.
clauses.summary: A consumer may request correction of inaccurate personal data.
A consumer may opt out of sale, targeted advertising, or profiling.

clauses.notes: Stated purpose language is checkable; operational minimization is not.
clauses.summary: Duty of purpose specification, data minimization, and duty of care.

clauses.notes: Assessments are internal. Policy text cannot prove one exists.
clauses.summary: Data protection assessment required for processing sensitive data.

clauses.notes: Vendor-processor contracts are not public policy text.
clauses.summary: Processor duties and contract requirements for processing personal data.

clauses.notes: Applicability is a facts-and-figures question, not a policy clause.
clauses.summary: CPA applicability thresholds (consumers, revenue, or revenue-from-sale).

clauses.citation: C.R.S. § 6-1-1308 (processing duties) applied to device telemetry
clauses.notes: Requires operator-owned device observation. Gated; off in Phase 0.
clauses.summary: Whether neural signals leave the device contrary to stated purpose.
Neural data means information generated by measuring activity of a consumer's central or peripheral nervous system that is not inferred from non-neural information.
Neural data is added to the sensitive personal information list.
Notice at collection must identify SPI categories collected.
Privacy policy must list SPI categories collected.
Consumer right to limit use and disclosure of sensitive personal information.
Right to opt out of sale or sharing of personal information.

clauses.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140 neural-data definition (non-inference clause)
clauses.notes: Whether a vendor infers 'focus' from clickstream is not in the privacy policy.
clauses.summary: Neural data does not include information inferred from non-neural information.
Service-provider contracts must restrict SPI use.

clauses.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.199.40 et seq. (CPPA / AG enforcement)
clauses.notes: Enforcement posture is not a vendor-policy fact.
clauses.summary: Enforcement is by the Agency and the Attorney General.

clauses.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.121 applied to on-device neural streams
clauses.notes: Optional, operator-owned devices only. Off in Phase 0.
clauses.summary: Whether SPI use is limited in the running product, not only in the policy.

decision: 14/22 = 0.636 of encoded provisions are machine-checkable from policy text. Phase 2 should center on extraction + deterministic scoring. Network capture stays optional.
